newsitem.title: USA: US Mid-Atlantic daily power down, deferreds steady.
newsitem.headline: US Mid-Atlantic daily power down, deferreds steady.

text.p: Day-ahead bulk electricity prices in the Mid-Atlantic U.S. fell Tuesday, continuing recent weakness due to falling natural gas prices and declining demand after last weekend's cold snap.

Although several coal-fired generating units, with total capacity of about 1,500 megawatts (MW), were heard shut for unplanned repairs since this weekend, there was little concern over decreased production due to the lackluster power usage.
"The load is pretty moderate," said a trader who deals in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect pool.
Firm, peak PJM electricity prices for Wednesday (excluding transmission costs) slipped to $24.00-$26.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) from Monday's $26.00-$27.00 for delivery today.
Firm, off-peak PJM power for Wednesday delivery tumbled to $13.00-$14.00 from $16.00-$18.00 Monday.
Today's hourly dispatch rate in PJM was last pegged near $17.00 versus Monday's peak that briefly touched $35.00.

Forecasts showed the midsection of the eastern seaboard would warm considerably Wednesday and Thursday with scattered showers and rain expected and temperatures running five to 12 degrees Fahrenheit above normal. Then, a cool front would push readings toward winter norms this weekend.

Temperatures in the PJM region were predicted to approach near normal winter level Tuesday and Wednesday after average 15-20 degrees Fahrenheit below normal over the weekend. Forecasts showed another cold wave would hit PJM later this week with readings running eight to 15 degrees below normal.
The natural gas market was hit with another round of heavy losses on outlook of above-normal temperatures across the country next week.
Swing gas values at the Philadelphia city gate were notionally pegged near $3.40 per million British thermal units, down from Monday's $4.25.
As of 1231 EST, NYMEX Henry Hub gas futures for February delivery plummeted 19.5 cents to $2.875/mmBtu.
Despite the ongoing decline in day-ahead prices, PJM deferred values held steady against Monday's levels.
February PJM electricity was quoted at $28.60-$29.25, compared with Monday's $28.75-$29.25, with deals reportedly done at $28.85.
March PJM electricity tightened to $24.10-$24.20 from $24.00-$24.25 Monday.
PJM deliveries April and May firmed to $22.00-$22.50 from Monday's $21.50-$22.00.
June power prices in PJM were notionally assessed at $25.25-$25.50 from $25.00-$25.25 Monday.
July/August PJM deliveries stablized after Monday's sharp drop, last quoted at $30.40-$30.80 compared with yesterday's $30.50-$30.80 range.
